why: Tsukiomi Genichiro's (speaker for resource 2812250) signature iaido style, named after an abbreviation that web research confirms stands for the term already locked as 'Jovian Federation' in this project's glossary. dialogue_13656 and dialogue_13667 both reference this named style/technique but could not fit the full name inside their hard byte budgets (26 and 22 visible characters respectively) alongside the sentence meaning, so both were compressed to generic phrasing ('Not an assassin's blade.' / 'My style can't win...!'). Proposing 'Jovian iaido' and 'Jovian Softness' as working English names for the technique family, for use where a full byte budget is not in force (unit bios, flavor text) and for central glossary review.

term_romaji: shijin / shijin homophone pun (poet vs. a dead person)
why: The source's signature joke for Izumi Maki puns her self-styled title 'the poet Maki' against 'Maki... the shijin', where the Japanese word 'shijin' is a homophone of both 'poet' and 'corpse/dead person'. No English homophone pair exists; substituted the portmanteau 'dead-et' (poet/dead) to keep the wordplay and the character's morbid self-deprecating humor within the row's byte budget. This is a creative equivalence rather than a literal translation - flagging for central review, especially if this specific joke recurs in other resources referencing Izumi.
